blocks.name: Scalar & vector quantities
blocks.definition: Understand that a scalar quantity has magnitude (size) only and that a vector quantity has magnitude and direction

blocks.md:
- All quantities can be one of two types:

  - A **scalar**
  - A **vector**

- Scalar quantities have only a ***magnitude***

  - **Mass** is an example of a scalar quantity because it has magnitude **without direction**
  - **Energy **and** time** are also examples of scalar quantities

- Vector quantities have both **magnitude** and **direction**

  - **Weight **is an example of a vector quantity because it is a **force **and therefore has both **magnitude **and **direction**
  - **Acceleration **and** momentum **are also examples of vector quantities

- **Distance **is a measure of how far an object has travelled, **regardless of direction**

  - Distance is the total length of the path taken
  - Distance, therefore, has a **magnitude **but **no direction**
  - So, distance is a **scalar **quantity

- **Displacement **is the distance between two points in a straight line, **in a stated direction**

  - So, displacement is a **vector **quantity

blocks.alt: Diagram comparing distance and displacement: a curved path between two points showing the total distance travelled, and a straight arrow between the same two points showing displacement.
blocks.caption: Displacement is a vector quantity, while distance is a scalar quantity

blocks.md:
- **Speed **is a measure of the **distance **travelled by an object per unit time, **regardless of the direction**

  - So, speed is a **scalar **quantity

- **Velocity **is the **speed** of an object **in a given direction**

  - So, velocity is a **vector **quantity

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
Make sure you are comfortable with the differences between **similar** scalars and vectors.

The most commonly confused pairings tend to be:

- speed and velocity
- mass and weight

blocks.name: Examples of scalars & vectors
blocks.definition:
Know that the following quantities are scalars:
   distance, speed, time, mass, energy and temperature
Know that the following quantities are vectors:
force, weight, velocity, acceleration, momentum, electric field strength and gravitational field strength

blocks.md:

blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
State what is meant by a scalar quantity and give two examples.

[3]

**Answer:**

**Step 1: Recall the definition of a scalar quantity**

- Scalars are quantities that have only a magnitude **[1 mark]**

**Step 2: Name two examples of scalar quantities**

Any **two** from:

- Distance
- Speed
- Time
- Mass
- Energy
- Temperature

**[2 marks]**
